name: Obsidian
notes: Arch's official extra repo packages Obsidian directly (not an AppImage wrapper); this is a vendor/noncore application under Obsidian's own proprietary license. Sync, plugins, and vault location remain yours to configure.

name: Syncthing
notes: Peer-to-peer file sync; Arch extra repo. Pairing devices, folder shares, and the Android companion app are manual steps this setup never performs. The `syncthing.service` user unit is not enabled automatically.

name: Thunderbird
notes: Mail and calendar client; Arch extra repo. Accounts, mail, and calendar sync are yours to configure; none are imported.

name: Satty
notes: Wayland screenshot annotation tool, typically piped from grim/slurp; Arch extra repo. No screenshot keybinding is configured by this setup.

name: Podman
notes: Daemonless, rootless-by-default container engine; Arch extra repo. Unlike Docker Engine, rootless `podman run`/`podman build` need no group membership, systemd service, or privilege escalation, so this installs like any other package. Rootless mode relies on per-user `/etc/subuid`/`/etc/subgid` ranges; modern `useradd`/`systemd-sysusers` allocate these automatically for normal user accounts. The optional Docker-API-compatible socket (`systemctl --user enable --now podman.socket`) is not enabled by this setup; see README for tools that need it.

name: podman-docker
notes: Emulates the `docker` and `docker-compose` CLI as thin wrappers over Podman; Arch extra repo, split from the podman package (pulls in podman as a dependency). Conflicts with the real `docker` package, which is not in this catalog. CLI-argument compatibility only: it does not by itself expose the Docker Engine HTTP API socket that some third-party TUIs expect (see podman's own entry and README).

name: podman-compose
notes: Runs docker-compose.yml files against Podman instead of Docker; Arch extra repo.

name: micro
notes: Arch extra repo.

name: Helix
notes: Modal terminal text editor with built-in LSP, tree-sitter highlighting, and fuzzy pickers; Arch extra repo. Binary is hx. Deploys a Dracula-Sakura theme (~/.config/helix/themes/dracula-sakura.toml, selected by ~/.config/helix/config.toml); Ryoku does not ship its own Helix config the way it does for Neovim, so this is a plain literal path, not a user_edits overlay.

name: omp
notes: Official release executables published for Linux x86_64 and arm64.

name: Kiro
notes: Official universal Linux tarballs. SHA-256 values were computed from the versioned vendor downloads. Kiro/bin/kiro is the CLI launcher and Kiro/kiro is the Electron desktop executable. The user-local install relies on unprivileged user namespaces for Chromium sandboxing because its chrome-sandbox helper cannot be installed root-owned setuid; --no-sandbox is not used.

name: Dracula Sakura wallpaper
notes: Wallhaven-hosted artwork (original by Ornimid, via Pixiv) whose dominant colors (#424153, #ea4c88, #993399) match the Dracula-Sakura palette's base/rose/lilac. Applied via `ryogami wallpaper set` so Ryoku's matugen pipeline derives the live desktop palette from it; this is an approximation of theme/palette.json, not an exact static colorscheme. Wallhaven purity rating is sketchy, not SFW.

name: llama.cpp w/ vulkan
notes: Arch's official extra-repo build, compiled natively against Arch's current openssl (no OpenSSL 3/4 soname mismatch the way upstream's prebuilt Ubuntu binaries had). ggml's backend acceleration is split into optional packages; runtime_libs installs ggml-vulkan so llama-cli/llama-server can use the Vulkan backend. Installation must still pass a runtime smoke check: a working host Vulkan driver is required, and this does not substitute a CPU-only build.
